You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — former TerraForm Global, Inc. business realized record after the merger, ~3-5-year horizon (~2020-2022)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. Because the acquired entity deregistered, this
> record is traced through the acquirer's own subsequent SEC filings, which separately
> name and describe the acquired business. This sub-dossier contains no information
> about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status after the transaction (feasibility-relevant)
- TerraForm Global, Inc.'s last periodic reports on EDGAR (CIK 1620702) were a Form
  10-K for fiscal year 2016 (filed 2017-06-15) and a Form 10-Q for Q3 2017 (filed
  2017-11-08); on January 8, 2018 the entity filed a Form 15-12B certifying termination
  of registration of its common stock and suspension of its reporting duty under the
  Exchange Act. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950157-18-000059, Form 15-12B]
- No Form 10-K or 20-F was filed by CIK 1620702 after deregistration. [SRC: https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001620702&type=10-K]
- The acquirer, Brookfield Renewable Partners L.P. (CIK 1533232, an SEC 20-F filer),
  separately names and describes the acquired business in its own subsequent annual
  reports, providing a traceable post-close record. [SRC: SEC accession 0001533232-21-000009, Form 20-F FY2020]

## Realized business record under the acquirer (named "TerraForm Global" business)
- Brookfield Renewable's Form 20-F for fiscal year 2020 (filed 2021-02-26) states that,
  "as part of the acquisition of TerraForm Global in December 2017," it acquired 294.4
  MW of wind facilities in the State of Bahia, Brazil, and that the December 2017
  acquisition "marked our entry into the wind and solar markets" in both India (66
  employees, none covered by collective agreements) and China (approximately 95
  employees, 13% covered by collective agreements). [SRC: SEC accession 0001533232-21-000009, Form 20-F FY2020]
- The same filing states that in March 2020 Brookfield Renewable "extended a $45
  million non-recourse revolving credit facility associated with our TerraForm Global
  business." [SRC: SEC accession 0001533232-21-000009, Form 20-F FY2020]

## Documented divestitures within the window (Note 4, Disposal of Assets)
- In March 2020, Brookfield Renewable, together with institutional partners, sold a 39
  MW solar portfolio in Thailand (part of the original 2017 acquired footprint) for
  total consideration of THB 3,079 million ($94 million); Brookfield Renewable's
  interest was approximately 31%, and the sale resulted in a loss on disposition of $12
  million ($4 million net to Brookfield Renewable). The portfolio had been classified
  as held-for-sale since 2018. [SRC: SEC accession 0001533232-21-000009, Form 20-F FY2020, Note 4]
- In September 2020, Brookfield Renewable sold its interest in a 33 MW solar facility in
  South Africa for gross cash consideration of ZAR 300 million ($18 million; $25 million
  total net proceeds after foreign-exchange contract settlements, $8 million net to
  Brookfield Renewable), resulting in a $4 million loss on disposition; this portfolio
  had also been classified as held-for-sale since 2018. [SRC: SEC accession 0001533232-21-000009, Form 20-F FY2020, Note 4]
- The FY2020 20-F states that "in 2020, Brookfield Renewable completed the sale of its
  non-core assets from the TerraForm Global portfolio in South Africa and Thailand,
  corresponding to 72 MW of solar assets." [SRC: SEC accession 0001533232-21-000009, Form 20-F FY2020]
- As of December 31, 2020, a remaining 19 MW solar portfolio in Malaysia (also part of
  the original acquired footprint) was classified as an asset held for sale. [SRC: SEC accession 0001533232-21-000009, Form 20-F FY2020]

## Later-window status (FY2021 20-F, filed 2022-03-01)
- The FY2021 20-F states Brookfield Renewable "entered into an agreement to sell" the
  Malaysia solar portfolio, indicating the sale agreed but not yet completed as of that
  filing; it reports 6 employees in Malaysia, 5 in Uruguay, and 4 in Chile at that date.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001533232-22-000007, Form 20-F FY2021]
- The FY2021 20-F's narrative business descriptions of the India, China, and Brazil
  operations no longer name "TerraForm Global" as the acquired-business label in the
  way the FY2020 filing did; the term appears only in the defined-terms glossary and a
  debt-structure reference to a successor entity, "TerraForm Global Holdco LLC."
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001533232-22-000007, Form 20-F FY2021]

## Items sought but not found
- No source was found separately reporting a divestiture, write-down, or comparable
  scalar for the Brazil (Bahia wind) or India/China assets within the window; the
  documented divestitures are limited to the South Africa and Thailand solar assets
  (2020) and the pending Malaysia sale. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- Because the acquired entity deregistered in January 2018, there is no periodic filing
  of its own for the ~2020-2022 window; the traceable realized record instead comes
  from the acquirer's (Brookfield Renewable Partners L.P.) own Form 20-F filings, which
  separately name and describe the acquired business through FY2020 and FY2021.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001533232-21-000009, Form 20-F FY2020; SEC accession 0001533232-22-000007, Form 20-F FY2021]
- Within the window, two of the original seven acquired geographic markets (Thailand
  and South Africa, together 72 MW) were sold at a combined disclosed loss on
  disposition of $16 million ($8 million net to Brookfield Renewable), and a third
  (Malaysia, 19 MW) was agreed to be sold but remained unclosed by the FY2021 filing;
  the remaining India, China, and Brazil operations continued to be reported, with
  declining standalone naming of the business as "TerraForm Global" in the parent's
  public narrative by FY2021. [SRC: SEC accession 0001533232-21-000009, Form 20-F FY2020; SEC accession 0001533232-22-000007, Form 20-F FY2021]

[SLICE END]
